entry.title: Physical AI System Design for Supply Chain and Logistics: What the Published Designs Already Answer
entry.summary: No supply chain design has been published in this series yet. Eight of the eighteen open reference architectures already answer the questions a logistics network asks first: one picture across the nodes from the systems they already run, gate and yard turn time, whether a terminal's inventory reading can be trusted, which vehicle in the fleet is raising a fault, what is connected to the control networks at each site, counting what moves, incidents before they happen, and what a records only study can settle before any sensor is bought.

entry.title: What Does It Take to Vibe Code a Truck?
entry.summary: Software can now be described into existence. Physical systems cannot, because the knowledge needed to design them lives in the heads of senior engineers. This is how CodeNinja Atoms is building the missing piece: deep domain expertise for physical AI system design, carried as context instead of trained into weights.

entry.title: Physical AI System Design for Semiconductors: What the Published Designs Already Answer
entry.summary: No semiconductor design has been published in this series yet. Nine of the eighteen open reference architectures already answer the questions a fab or a packaging and test plant asks first: one picture of the operation from the systems it already runs, subfab and facility equipment condition, what is connected to the control networks and how to prove it, bulk tank readings that can be trusted, fire and life safety, people near equipment on camera, incidents before they happen, counting what leaves, and what a records only study can settle before any sensor is bought.

entry.title: From a CISA Advisory to a Closed Finding
entry.summary: What an operational technology security team does with an advisory about an actively exploited vulnerability, traced through one published system of context: the advisory becomes a threat intelligence item, the item seeds detection rules, a finding scores the operator's own assets, a named analyst accepts or rejects the risk, and the evidence a NERC CIP audit asks for is assembled on the way.

entry.title: The Model Register Across Sixteen Designs
entry.summary: Sixteen open reference architectures for physical operations, each with a model register the operator owns outright. Twelve models, four empty registers by decision, and one licence pattern that repeats in every design.

entry.title: Sensing Comes Before the Model
entry.summary: Three published earth observation architectures decide what to watch from law, revisit and ownership, never from model accuracy. Two of the three ship with an empty model register.

entry.title: Own or Rent the GPUs
entry.summary: Seven published reference architectures, priced the same way, say owning the reasoning node costs between about half and nearly all of the deepest three year cloud commitment. Not a tenth.

entry.title: Don't Baptize the GPUs
entry.summary: Why AI systems should be measured by running them, trained to seek truth and owned by the organizations that depend on them, rather than blessed into a theological category.
